study: Five individually literature-traceable alloy corrosion-rate benchmarks mapped to the user-supplied ten-body drum
scopeWarning: These are NOT measured under identical conditions. Use as separate literature-benchmark transfers only. Not 60C/3bar H2S corrosion predictions for five alloys and not an evidence-based material ranking.

6061_T6.label: Al 6061-T6
6061_T6.method: Uncoated/reference 6061-T6 polarization j_corr in Table 3; approximate ASTM G102 conversion, i_corr=9.47 µA/cm², EW=26.9815385/3 g/equiv, density=2.70 g/cm³; not an experimentally observed uniform penetration depth
6061_T6.environment: Aqueous 3.5 wt% NaCl; no intentionally added H₂S; study of anodizing vs uncoated reference
6061_T6.sourceTitle: Effect of Citric Acid Hard Anodizing on the Mechanical Properties and Corrosion Resistance of Different Aluminum Alloys (Materials, 2024), Table 3
6061_T6.limitation: No H2S test; equivalent-weight approximation assumes aluminum predominantly dissolves as Al3+, not exact alloy stoichiometry; positive polarization hysteresis suggests localized attack could make Faraday uniform-depth proxy underestimate pit depth.

7075_T6.label: Al 7075-T6
7075_T6.method: Uncoated/reference 7075-T6 polarization j_corr from same Table 3 as 6061-T6; approximate ASTM G102 conversion, i_corr=0.31 µA/cm², EW=26.9815385/3 g/equiv, density=2.81 g/cm³
7075_T6.environment: Same 3.5 wt% aqueous NaCl study as Al 6061-T6; no intentionally added H₂S
7075_T6.sourceTitle: Effect of Citric Acid Hard Anodizing on the Mechanical Properties and Corrosion Resistance of Different Aluminum Alloys (Materials, 2024), Table 3
7075_T6.limitation: This low electrochemical current is not proof of wet sour-service suitability. Positive hysteresis suggests localized corrosion; converted mm/y is an approximate uniform-equivalent rate only.

1020_NORMALIZED.label: AISI 1020 candidate (normalized)
1020_NORMALIZED.testedGrade: AISI 1020 (normalization heat treatment NOT confirmed in paper)
1020_NORMALIZED.method: Seven-day gravimetric weight loss for the smoothest 2400-grit specimen in Table 5; paper also reports 0.92 ± 0.06 mm/y at 100-grit and intermediate values, all in CO₂ brine, not H₂S.
1020_NORMALIZED.environment: 25°C, CO₂-saturated 3 wt% NaCl, pH ~5, atmospheric pressure, stagnant 168 hours (7 days), 2400-grit
1020_NORMALIZED.sourceTitle: Mechanistic Role of Surface Roughness on CO₂ Corrosion Kinetics and Pitting Susceptibility of AISI 1020 Carbon Steel (International Journal of Design & Nature and Ecodynamics, 2026), Table 5
1020_NORMALIZED.limitation: CO2, not H2S; temperature 25C, not 60C; exact normalized state not verified; value corresponds to smooth sample and is not a material-wide minimum.

AISI_304.label: AISI 304
AISI_304.method: Author-reported stainless steel substrate corrosion rate in abstract; Cr3C2–25NiCr coating reported 72% lower rate than stainless steel substrate.
AISI_304.environment: Simulated H₂S-containing oil/gas field medium; complete test temperature, H₂S partial pressure and solution chemistry not available from accessible abstract
AISI_304.sourceTitle: Assessment of Sulfide Corrosion and Wear Behavior of HVOF-Sprayed Cr3C2–25NiCr Coating on 304 Stainless Steels in H2S Environment (Transactions of the Indian Institute of Metals, 2023)
AISI_304.limitation: Only abstract verified; precise temperature/H2S pressure not established. Do not assume its 0.17 mm/y rate applies to 3 bar H2S or to untested surface finish.

AISI_316.label: AISI 316 candidate (316L proxy)
AISI_316.method: Seven-day 316L weight-loss corrosion at 3-bar H2S from 2020 paper; as-used candidate 316 differs in composition/carbon limit.
AISI_316.environment: 60°C, H₂S partial pressure 3 bar, total pressure 30 bar, 5 wt% NaCl + 0.5 wt% acetic acid, pH ~3, 7-day immersion
AISI_316.sourceTitle: The Effect of H₂S Pressure on the Formation of Multiple Corrosion Products on 316L Stainless Steel Surface (Shah et al., 2020)
AISI_316.limitation: Measured on 316L not AISI 316; weight-loss corrosion is not deepest pit or SSC/HIC qualification.

method.baselineRate: ONE chosen published/converted literature benchmark per material. No low/central/high assigned hypotheses.
method.mode1: Uniform whole-surface literature benchmark, r_i = base_rate(material); no hypothetical hotspots.
method.mode2: Illustrative chamber hotspot overlay on top of the same literature benchmark. Local r_i = base_rate(material)*(1+(F-1)*H_i), H_i inherited illustrative CAD field, F=2.4/0.74 from different 316L published studies; ONLY 316L has related measured pit/uniform evidence. Other alloys' local values are hypothetical and are NOT measured pit rates.
method.pitSupport: 316L deepest-pit penetration 2.4 mm/y after 7d at 3 bar H2S from Shah et al., Trends in Sciences 2022; baseline 0.74 mm/y from a related 2020 316L study; ratio transferred to other materials only as clearly hypothetical shape overlay
method.loss: loss_i = r_i * exposure_days / 365, with constant-rate projection only
method.wall: Remaining chamber wall = max(0, 10mm - local inner loss - uniform outer loss); illustrated pairing, no exact wall-pair geometry
notCalculated: True H2S electrochemistry for all alloys
Actual pitting location or pit probability
